title: Open a drink can by its stay-on tab: slide a fingertip's edge under the tab's thin tail inside the lid's recess and lever it up until the seal breaks
context: Opening a drink can is something most people do every day. The stay-on tab is a lever riveted to the lid: lifting its tail presses its nose down on the scored panel until the seal breaks and the panel folds into the can (Wikipedia, Beverage can: the tab "uses a separate tab attached to the upper surface as a lever to depress a scored part of the lid"). The hard part is physical: the tail is a 1.5 mm curled edge lying 1.3 mm above a lid 4.6 mm below the rim, too thin and too close to the lid to pinch. A fingertip's edge has to be slid under it inside the rim, as a person does, and the tail levered up on its arc about the rivet until the seal breaks.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. One closed, ordinary 12 fl oz (355 ml) aluminium drink can with a standard 202 stay-on-tab end, red, 6.6 cm across and 12.27 cm tall, stands upright at (26, 0), held in place by a holder (it is fixed). For real trials: a Coca-Cola Classic 12 fl oz can (the standard 202/211 x 413 can), unmodified. Its lid panel is 5.1 cm across inside the rim and 4.6 mm below the rim's top. The stay-on tab lies flat on the lid at an ordinary tab's size: aluminium, 2.5 cm long and 1.57 cm wide, its edge curled to 1.5 mm thick, its underside 1.3 mm above the lid. It is riveted at the lid's centre, 0.8 cm from its nose's end and 1.7 cm from its tail's end. Its tail points away from the arms (+x); its nose lies over the scored panel (1.7 x 1.4 cm), which is on the side nearer the arms (-x). The tab has no added grip. Both grippers start open at the ready pose; each fingertip ends in a tongue 15.5 mm wide and 3.95 mm thick.
scoring: Measured on the can: how far the tab's tail has been raised about its rivet (the most this trial) and how far the panel is pushed into the can about its hinge, in degrees. 1.0: the panel in at least 45 degrees, the tab having been raised at least 10 degrees (it was the tab that opened it; it may be folded back down after), and both hands off the can (no finger pad or fingertip within 1.5 cm of it), held for 1 s, which ends the trial (if time runs out before that has held, it scores 0.9). 0.75: opened so, with a hand still on the can. 0.5: the seal broken (the panel in at least 10 degrees) with the tab raised at least 3 degrees. 0.25: the tab raised at least 10 degrees but the seal holding. 0 otherwise, including a panel poked in with the tab never raised, and any trial in which a fingertip goes below the rim's top on the opening's side of the rivet (over the tab's nose or the panel) while the seal still holds (the panel in less than 10 degrees): the can has to be opened by lifting the tab's tail, not by pressing the nose or the panel down.
reset_notes: Use a fresh closed can for every trial (chilled and not shaken, so it does not spray), its tab pointing away from the robot and its opening towards it; the holder keeps it from moving and catches drips.
fidelity: The can is fixed in place. The tab has a real tab's length, width, edge thickness and height off the lid (sources in the README); it and the panel are rigid plates on hinges, so the tab does not bend. The seal is a sprung catch the panel cams aside, not tearing metal: it gives way at a few newtons at the tail (estimated), less than a real end's 20 to 31 N. Tab and panel weigh 3 g each, heavier than real, for stable contacts. The lid is flat: no finger well or countersink groove.
